subject: Usage-driven dedicated GPU top-up request (Aperture Analytics)
messages:
From: Sam Park <sam@aperture.io>
To: Priya Natarajan <priya.natarajan@redwood.ai>
Cc: Jenna Liu <jenna.liu@aperture.io>, procurement@aperture.io
Date: Fri, 20 Nov 2026 09:13:00 -0800
Subject: Request: committed GPU top-up ahead of renewal (usage attached)

Hi Priya,

Thanks again for the walkthrough last month. We ran the synthetic load against the new encoder ensembles and wanted to share a short usage snapshot and ask about next steps for adding committed capacity. The attached CSV is a 30-day export from our usage dashboard (UTC timestamps, aggregated per-hour). Key signals:

- 95th-percentile sustained concurrency has moved from ~60 vGPUs to ~88 vGPUs over the last 6 weeks.
- Peak 1-hour windows show short bursts to ~130 vGPUs during campaign rollouts.
- Average utilization over the month is 62% but with consistent evening peaks (21:00–23:00 PT).

Our renewal is due in mid-December. We want to convert some of our burst into committed capacity to reduce per-token variability and the risk of throttled requests as we scale. Can Redwood propose a minimal committed tranche (GPUs + burst buffer) and the pricing delta to convert? Also please call out any recommended autoscale or KV cache settings you think will improve steady-state efficiency.

We attached the usage export; I can loop in procurement for contract phrasing once we have numbers.

Appreciate a quick turnaround — we’re trying to lock capacity before our Q4 campaign starts.

Best,
Sam
Director of ML Ops
Aperture Analytics

Attachment: util-report-nov2026.csv (CSV, 120KB)
From: Priya Natarajan <priya.natarajan@redwood.ai>
To: Sam Park <sam@aperture.io>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>, Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.ai>
Date: Mon, 23 Nov 2026 10:02:00 -08:00
Subject: Re: Request: committed GPU top-up ahead of renewal (usage attached)

Hi Sam — thanks for the data and clear ask.

Quick read of the CSV (thanks!) suggests a good opportunity to blend 1) a small committed tranche for baseline steady-state and 2) a controlled burst buffer to absorb campaign spikes. High level proposal we can put in writing:

- Baseline committed: 48 A100-equivalent vGPUs (covers 95% of non-peak hours at current efficiency with a 10% headroom).
- Burst/Bridge pool: additional 48 vGPUs available with pre-negotiated burst pricing and priority routing to your fleet.
- Autoscale policy: 15–90s scale windows for short bursts; keep continuous batching on and enable prefix KV caching for repeated prompts during campaigns.

I’ve looped in Ben and Karthik to get a tranche-level price and lead time. If that sounds reasonable, we’ll produce a formal amend (pricing/term impact) and a one-way conversion path for the burst to committed at the next renewal checkpoint.

Proposed next steps:
1) Redwood to send tranche amendment + pricing (Ben).
2) Aperture procurement to confirm internal approvals (Sam/procurement).
3) Target: sign amendment by Dec 10 to lock capacity ahead of the campaign.

Any constraints on region or IP? We’ll default to us-west for capacity.

Thanks — Priya
Priya Natarajan
Senior AE, Dedicated Accounts
Redwood Inference
From: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>
To: Priya Natarajan <priya.natarajan@redwood.ai>, Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.ai>
Cc: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa.ortiz@redwood.ai>
Date: Tue, 24 Nov 2026 08:37:00 -08:00
Subject: Pricing sketch: Aperture proposed tranche (draft)

Team — quick draft numbers for Priya/Aperture based on the 48+48 split and Aperture's current committed pricing band:

- 48 committed vGPUs (12-month add-on): $62,400/mo (list), with a 12% volume discount applied = $54,912/mo.
- 48 burst vGPUs (on-demand reserved buffer): $8,800/mo (reservation fee) + per-token burst surcharge (10% over committed rate) when used.
- One-time amendment fee: $2,500 for provisioning and SLA onboarding.
- SLA: 99.5% uptime for committed tranche; burst pool best-effort with priority queuing.

Notes/assumptions: 
- Pricing assumes A100-equivalent vGPUs and standard memory profile.
- We should include a clause for converting unused burst to committed at a pre-agreed conversion rate (e.g., 3 months of average daily burst usage triggers a conversion discount).
- Lead time: 7–10 business days from sign to capacity in us-west with the current provisioning queue.

Vanessa, please prepare the standard amendment PDF and call out the conversion mechanics (we'll reference HubSpot deal APTR-2026-RNW-42).

Ben
Account Executive — Strategic Growth
Redwood Inference

Attachment: proposed-tranche-amendment.pdf (PDF, 220KB)
From: Priya Natarajan <priya.natarajan@redwood.ai>
To: Sam Park <sam@aperture.io>, Jenna Liu <jenna.liu@aperture.io>, procurement@aperture.io
Cc: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>, Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.ai>, Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa.ortiz@redwood.ai>
Date: Thu, 26 Nov 2026 14:20:00 -08:00
Subject: Re: Request: committed GPU top-up ahead of renewal (usage attached)

Sam/Jenna — attaching the amendment and a short FAQ around conversion mechanics. Key items called out in the doc:

- Committed tranche: 48 vGPUs at the discounted committed rate.
- Burst pool: 48 vGPUs with reservation fee + surcharge when used.
- Conversion trigger: if rolling 90-day average usage of the burst pool > 30% for 45 consecutive days, Aperture can convert a portion of the burst at a 20% discount off the committed list price; conversion requires 30 days' notice.
- Lead time: 7–10 business days; we can prioritize if sign occurs by Dec 6.

Procurement: please confirm any PO process items or vendor form requirements so we can prep legal.

Next steps: if this is acceptable, sign the amendment and we’ll kick provisioning.  Priya will schedule a 30-minute runbook review with Infra to ensure autoscale/tuning settings (Karthik/SRE) are aligned prior to campaign start.

Best,
Priya

Attachment: proposed-tranche-amendment.pdf (PDF, 220KB)
From: Jenna Liu <jenna.liu@aperture.io>
To: Priya Natarajan <priya.natarajan@redwood.ai>, Sam Park <sam@aperture.io>
Cc: procurement@aperture.io, Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>
Date: Mon, 29 Nov 2026 15:42:00 -08:00
Subject: Re: Request: committed GPU top-up ahead of renewal (usage attached)

Thanks — this looks good. Procurement flagged two items: 1) need Redwood's SOC2 attestation link for the legal attachment, and 2) want the option to convert up to 20 vGPUs from burst to committed mid-term rather than waiting for the 45-day rolling trigger.

We can sign the amendment by Dec 4 if those two items are addressed. Can Redwood provide SOC2 attestation link and a short note on whether the 20 vGPU mid-term conversion can be accommodated as an added clause? If so, we’ll route this for final approval.

Appreciate the fast turnaround.

Jenna
VP Marketing
Aperture Analytics
